claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2013 reports: The Castries assessment identifies Black Mallet, Maynard Hill, Entrepot, Bocage and Pavee in Castries East, Bois Patat and Morne Dudon in Castries North, and La Pansee in Castries Central as poor, unplanned hillside settlements exposed to landslides.
claim_decisions.locator: 2013 report, physical PDF p.74, printed p.57, named hillside settlements; historical 2010–2012 indicators.

claim_decisions.statement: The March 2014 assessment reports that the December 2013 trough heavily affected Anse La Raye, Canaries, Soufriere, Micoud, Choiseul and Vieux Fort. More than 550 people were evacuated to shelters or other refuges, with poverty affecting vulnerability.
claim_decisions.locator: Original 66-page assessment, executive summary and social-impact discussion; printed pp.5–6, physical pp.19–20.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Historical event estimates, not current displacement. Some housing damage was not captured.

claim_decisions.statement: The 2013 trough damaged roads, bridges, John Compton Dam's water system and distribution pipes; some communities lacked piped water for up to ten days.
claim_decisions.locator: Original PDF physical p.20, printed p.6, water and transport disruption.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Historical disruption, not current service condition or an evaluated resilience outcome.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-05-01 reports: A 2026 UN consultation included Saint Lucia among countries shaping a regional response to youth crime and violence. The article says regional youth risks are linked to structural inequality, socioeconomic exclusion, weak protective environments and unmet psychosocial needs, especially for boys and young men.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Regional consultation diagnosis including Saint Lucia, not country-specific prevalence or a climate-caused violence finding.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-05-01 reports: The proposed regional programme targets ages 10-29 with public-health and socio-ecological prevention, youth participation and gender-responsive interventions; in May 2026 stakeholders were still validating its design and governance arrangements.

gaps: Main corrected physical versus printed PDF locator confusion in the 2014 event assessment. The 550-person figure describes evacuations, not an independently measured long-term displacement caseload.
No climate-violence or insecurity-to-adaptation causal chain was established. The subregional youth programme was still being designed, not an implemented climate-peace intervention.

executive_assessment.text: Castries has named historical hillside vulnerabilities, while the 2013 trough illustrates unequal exposure and water-service disruption. These are not current risk rankings.
DRR institutions and regional youth-violence programme design add institutional context, without establishing a climate-conflict link or delivered programme outcomes.
